//: The third train, added 2026-08-29. Its two packages — angulux-license-guard and
angulux-migrate — carry BARE npm names on purpose (see the scope decision in the brain:
outward-facing tools stay unscoped) and were published BY HAND at 1.0.0 on 2026-07-23,
nine minutes before the commit that introduced one of them even landed on main.
WHY THEY STOPPED BEING HAND-RELEASED. `release/rails.mjs` declared them in
RELEASED_BY_HAND, which was an honest record of a real decision and cost nothing until a
security fix had to reach users. A hand publish cannot produce a provenance attestation:
`npm publish --provenance` needs the OIDC token that only a workflow holds. So 'released
by hand' and 'every artifact we ship can be verified' could not both stay true, and the
second one is the argument this project is built on.
SEEDING, and why it is not optional. semantic-release derives the current version from
tags. With no `angulux-tools-v*` tag it computes 1.0.0 — which is exactly what both
manifests and the registry already say. The prepare step would then stamp a version
nothing changed, the workflow's before/after comparison would read 'no release',
the publish step is gated on that comparison and would be SKIPPED, and the run would go
green having published nothing while the tag was already pushed. Seeded at `d214aac`,
the commit that added angulux-migrate, which is the tree the published 1.0.0 was cut
from. release/README.md records the same trap for the other two trains.
No @semantic-release/git, for the reason spelled out in forks.releaserc.json: it commits
to `main`, which is protected, and the release commit carries [skip ci] so the required
check can never be satisfied. The tag and the GitHub release are the record.
commit-analyzer and release-notes-generator are wrapped by ./release/rail-filter.mjs so
this train reads only the commits that touched its own packages, from the one path list
in release/rails.mjs that the workflow's path gate reads too.
The prepare step calls set-rail-versions.mjs rather than set-fork-versions.mjs — the
latter hard-codes the four fork names and would stamp THEM with this train's version,
leaving both tool manifests untouched and producing exactly the silent skip described
above.
